distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.7579 +/- 0.0112 mas (same row, RUWE 0.97): 114.18 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.202 +/- 0.037 solar radii from Dugan et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1135 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJ...994L..23D/abstract): 836,231 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.119 +/- 0.069 solar masses from Dugan et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1135 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJ...994L..23D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6320 +/- 120 K from Dugan et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1135 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJ...994L..23D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Dugan et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1135 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJ...994L..23D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1135.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.327, rounded to two decimals
